name: Film finish — grade, optics, grain and HDR on the card
description: The presenter finishing look on the GPU, streamed frame by frame so a 4K take of any length fits: a grade in linear light, halation, a diffusion filter, lens aberration and vignette, film grain, then Rec.709 SDR, HDR10 (PQ) or HLG. `strong` is the original presenter look; clean, film and film-strong are graded from light. A reference take matches skin and exposure across takes. No model download.

licence.name: Pepper Pro's own node (comfy-nodes/pepper_finish); `expand: rtx` uses the NVIDIA Video Effects SDK
obligations: expand: rtx runs NVIDIA's proprietary VFX runtime (nvidia-vfx, installed with rtx-master's node pack): review NVIDIA's SDK terms before redistributing an image that bundles it.

params.name: look
params.label: Look
params.description: strong/medium/subtle: the presenter look picked on 2026-10-21 (the skill's former finish.py), on display values; its sizes scale with the frame's width, as finish.py's did, so a landscape take gets coarser halation and grain. film-strong/film: a print look from linear light (soft highlight roll-off, teal shadows, warm highlights, dense colour, halation, a Pro-Mist diffusion, lens aberration, film grain). clean: a matched commercial grade, no texture.

params.name: output
params.label: Output
params.description: sdr: Rec.709 H.264 (x264). hdr10: BT.2020 PQ HEVC 10-bit with mastering and light-level metadata, for YouTube. hlg: BT.2020 HLG HEVC 10-bit, for Instagram from the phone app. In HDR, SDR white sits at 203 nits and only highlights rise toward the peak.

params.name: expand
params.label: HDR highlights
params.description: curve: the grade's own highlight expansion (the HDR and SDR versions are the same grade). rtx: NVIDIA RTX Video HDR expands the graded SDR picture.

params.name: lut
params.label: LUT
params.description: A Rec.709-in, Rec.709-out creative .cube, uploaded as an input (never a log-input LUT: takes are display Rec.709). It replaces the look's grade; in HDR it drives the HDR picture too.

params.name: match
params.label: Match to take
params.description: A reference take (the hero take of the set): this take's skin tone and exposure are moved toward it, by at most a stop and 12% per channel.

params.name: encoder
params.label: Encoder
params.description: cpu: x264 slow / x265 medium, best for grain. fast: one preset quicker. gpu: NVENC, fastest, softens grain. Without NVENC in the container, gpu falls back to fast and says so in the report.

finish.label: Finish
finish.description: One pass: decode, the look on the GPU, encode.

notes: Runs on any CUDA card (and MPS or the CPU, slowly, for checks). The x264/x265 encode on the CPU sets the speed, not the GPU: the three stages run at once. RTX highlights need an NVIDIA RTX card and rtx-master's node pack (nvidia-vfx).
